title: Service interface stability & compatibility jam notes
content:
Meeting: Service interface stability & compatibility — engineering jam
Date: 2026-02-18 10:00–11:15 PT
Location: Zoom / #platform-arch slack
Facilitator: Ethan Chen
Attendees: Leah Ortiz, Marcus Li, Priya Nair, Jonah Park, Ava Martinez, Samir Gupta (guest: product-hosted-api), remote: Noor Alvi (observability)
Context / Why we met:
- There have been three recent incidents where minor protocol changes caused cascading client-side regressions in Dedicated and Private deployments. We want a concrete compatibility policy + short-term mitigations to reduce customer impact while we work on long-term API contract tooling.
- Goals: land a minimal, enforceable compatibility contract; decide on compatibility modes and server-side enforcement; identify rollout and test automation needs.
Notes / overview:
1) Problem statement recap
   - Small changes (header presence, enum value additions) have caused 2–5% traffic failures for some customers during canary rollouts. Not catastrophic but noisy and increases support load.
   - Current client libraries accept some changes but not others; no single source of truth for acceptable change classes.
   - We lack automated pre-rollout compatibility checks that exercise private deployment edge cases (networking, KMS behavior).
2) Compatibility taxonomy proposed (short summary)
   - Safe additive: adding optional fields, new enum values (clients should ignore unknowns).
   - Safe removal with deprecation: removing fields after deprecation window and client adoption check.
   - Breaking: required field type changes, removal without deprecation, semantic changes to response meaning.
   - Behavioral: changes in streaming semantics, chunk boundaries, or retry hints. May require policy-specific testing.
3) Enforcement model options discussed
   A) Soft enforcement: server emits compatibility warnings in response metadata and console alerts during canary windows. No immediate reject.
   B) Hard enforcement: gateway rejects requests that violate declared compatibility policy for a release channel.
   C) Compatibility testing pipeline: automated contract checks using recorded client interactions + golden responses before rollout.
   - Tradeoffs: A is fast but only informs; B is safest for customers but increases risk for deploy velocity; C requires investment but reduces surprises long term.
4) Decision (consensus)
   - Adopt a hybrid path: start with A + C in parallel. Implement soft enforcement (warnings + console/Slack alerts) for next two sprints; build a scoped compatibility test harness (C) targeting the highest-risk APIs and private deployment permutations. Revisit hard enforcement (B) after 3 months and when coverage for C reaches ~70%.
   - Rationale: immediate customer protection with minimal rollout friction, while working toward automated prevention. B will be evaluated only once tests provide sufficient coverage to avoid false positives.
5) Compatibility modes and API-level gating
   - Introduce release-channel headers: X-RW-Release-Channel (stable/canary/experimental). Server will include compatibility-warnings in X-RW-Compat header when soft enforcement detects questionable changes.
   - Define per-API compatibility metadata stored in model-service catalog (small JSON schema) indicating allowed change classes per field. This metadata is the input to the test harness.
6) Implementation plan (next 6 weeks)
   Sprint 1 (weeks 1–2):
     - Add X-RW-Compat header generation on the gateway and internal routes (Marcus Li) — prototype by 2026-02-26.
     - Create a light-weight UI panel in Console showing recent compatibility warnings for a model/API (Priya Nair) — mockups by 2026-02-25.
     - Add logging hook to capture client-side error types tied to compat warnings (Leah Ortiz) — telemetry ticket JIRA-ENG-8721.
   Sprint 2 (weeks 3–4):
     - Implement compatibility metadata schema and a small catalog (Jonah Park) — draft schema 2026-03-08.
     - Build unit-level contract checks for model-service responses using golden fixtures (Samir & platform-eng intern) — initial tests 2026-03-12.
   Sprint 3 (weeks 5–6):
     - Integrate contract checks into CI and pre-rollout pipelines for canary channel (E2E with Private VPC permutations) (Noor & SRE) — target 2026-03-25.
     - Run two internal canaries with soft enforcement enabled, measure false-positive rate and developer feedback.
7) Observability and metrics to track
   - number_of_compat_warnings emitted by channel
   - downstream_client_error_rate within 5 minutes of compat warning
   - mean_time_to_detect_and_notify (tools -> oncall -> eng owner)
   - false_positive_rate of automated contract checks once C is live
8) Rollout policy and customer communication
   - For next 90 days, default to soft enforcement for all channels. Account teams will be notified via automated emails when compat warnings exceed threshold for a customer.
   - Draft a short one-pager for CS/AMs explaining compatibility modes and recommended client library upgrades (Priya -> draft 2026-02-28).
9) Open questions / unresolved items
   - How do we version compatibility metadata? (schema v1 vs v2 migration plan) — Jonah to propose a lightweight incremental versioning approach by 2026-03-05.
   - Should SDKs automatically opt into ignoring unknown enum values or throw? Need coordination across SDK owners. Leah to run a compatibility survey across SDK repos (js/py/go) by 2026-02-27.
   - Private deployments: how to get telemetry back from air-gapped installs for warnings? Short term: rely on support/agent debug uploads; long term: consider optional telemetry proxy. Assigned to Marcus + solutions-eng for a feasibility note by 2026-03-10.
   - What threshold triggers escalation to hard enforcement? Proposed metric: sustained compat warning rate >0.5% of requests for 1 hour in stable channel. Keep open for further calibration.
10) Action items (owners + due dates)
   - Marcus Li: prototype X-RW-Compat header & gateway hook, demo 2026-02-26.
   - Priya Nair: Console mockups + CS one-pager draft, 2026-02-28.
   - Leah Ortiz: telemetry hook + SDK compatibility survey (js/py/go), 2026-02-27.
   - Jonah Park: metadata schema draft + versioning proposal, 2026-03-05.
   - Noor Alvi / SRE: run internal canary plan for sprint 3, 2026-03-25.
   - Samir Gupta: golden fixtures for top 5 model APIs, 2026-03-12.
   - Solutions Eng (Marcus + Priya): feasibility note for private-deploy telemetry, 2026-03-10.
Appendix / short notes from discussion:
- Priya: emphasized that Console visibility is high-impact for non-engineering stakeholders; make warning details human-readable (link to sample payload + suggested mitigation steps).
- Leah: recommended SDK semver guidance and a short compatibility test harness that can be run locally by SDK developers.
- Marcus: noted potential performance overhead of deep response diffs; suggested sampling at 1% to start.
- Jonah: suggested storing metadata alongside model artifacts in the artifact registry so compatibility metadata travels with model versions.
- Noor: asked that we add a synthetic test for KMS-induced response variance as part of the Private VPC permutation tests.
Closing / next sync:
- Weekly sync on Fridays 9:00 PT to check progress on action items, starting 2026-02-20.
- Re-evaluate strict enforcement decision after CI contract coverage reaches 70% OR after three canary cycles, whichever comes first.

Notes-to-self / scribbles (informal):
- Possible short-term hack: a feature-flag to strip new non-required fields in stable channel responses during rollout (dangerous but could be used for emergency mitigation).
- Keep communication templates ready for CS so they can proactively reach customers during canary blips.

References and links (copy into Confluence later):
- Compatibility taxonomy proposal (internal doc) -> CONFLUENCE-PLAT-1234
- Telemetry ticket -> JIRA-ENG-8721
- Gateway compat header PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/410
- Platform API catalog PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform-api/pull/222

End of notes.
